bounds: One runtime with five effective availability states and separate load, outcome and finally phases. The failure count saturates at the first 30-second delay, so repeated capped failures can continue without a bound on attempt count. Logical ticks count whole elapsed seconds. A wall-clock change is a stutter. The ownership case uses two coordinator records for one runtime, an active-map identity, five effective service availability values and a binary cooldown abstraction. Publication can release a mapped record before its callback or finally completes.
fairness: The host load and its finally callback must settle. The monotonic clock must advance to exhaust a pending cooldown.
limitations: Service publication, unload and replacement may overlap two coordinator records. Registry generations and service instance teardown retain their separate RuntimeLifecycle and ServiceLifecycle models.

The numeric case projects wall-clock changes away and uses elapsed seconds. The ownership case abstracts the precise delay to cooling or elapsed. The SQLite suite covers the monotonic millisecond boundary and repeated capped delays.
Actual log, runtime-error and agent-error observers can throw while recovery reports a failure. Their existing diagnostics boundaries preserve the coordinator record and cooldown.
Independent runtimes and cross-process recovery are outside this per-runtime ownership case.

assumptions: No scheduling fairness. External availability changes are restricted to idle states.
The host service load eventually resolves or rejects and its finally callback runs.
Weak fairness of monotonic elapsed-time ticks while a cooldown is active.
No scheduling fairness. A cooldown can persist while elapsed time does not advance.
No fairness. A delayed successful callback may release only its own currently mapped coordinator record.
No fairness. A failed callback writes only its own record, including when a replacement record is mapped.
No fairness. Finally clears only the callback owner’s in-flight marker.

Weak fairness of each owner’s completion actions. Admitted load receipt delivery and finally callbacks eventually complete. Diagnostic observer exceptions are caught by the actual logger, runtime and agent-event boundaries.
